purpose: Avoid the unconditional third-party comment bootstrap on ordinary article visits while preserving existing discussion identity and login returns.
publication: Draft only. PR72 remains separately pending and is not included.

scope.loadTrigger: Explicit reader click or an Utterances login-return parameter.
scope.fallback: Existing repository issue search using the unchanged legacyUrl/translationKey term.

review.type: Self AI review of loader state transitions, protocol source, localized action/status strings, keyboard behavior and controlled/real browser checks.

findings.issue: The existing async script is fetched even when the reader never opens comments; the provider already lazily loads its frame.
findings.resolution: Defer the bootstrap itself. State the measured client-request change without claiming every iframe was previously eager or that field performance improved.

findings.issue: Deferral could interrupt an explicit comment-login return or change the issue mapping.
findings.resolution: Automatically open only a nonempty Utterances return parameter; keep the exact legacyUrl || translationKey choice, repository and theme.

findings.issue: Duplicate activation, failures or an untrusted message could complete loading incorrectly.
findings.resolution: Guard one activation, accept resize only from the current iframe at the exact provider origin, and expose the GitHub fallback on failure or20-second timeout.

findings.issue: Disabling a focused native button can lose keyboard focus while loading.
findings.resolution: Use aria-disabled with the activation guard; transfer focus only if it remains on the initiating button, otherwise preserve the reader’s current focus.

findings.issue: No-JavaScript users need a usable discussion route without a dead button.
findings.resolution: Hide the action until initialized and keep a localized GitHub link in the static HTML.

translationReview.review: Two-pass self review of action/progress/completion/failure meaning and natural UI wording. This does not certify the external widget’s own language.

controlledBrowserCases.case: origin and frame source guards; reader focus retained

screenshotsReviewed: KO320px opened state with a controlled comment frame.
validation.timeoutNote: The controlled timeout case shortened only the20-second timer to80ms through a browser test hook; production code retains20seconds.

limits: No Google search/ranking or field Core Web Vitals effect is measured.
The real smoke check opened the widget without signing in or sending a comment.
The login-return and failure cases use controlled responses and do not perform a real OAuth login.
Reader-triggered widget requests still depend on the external service.
Only action/status strings are localized; the third-party frame UI is unchanged.
